title: Notebook: one secret in source, stream, result, JSON bundle, error and traceback
summary: A synthetic two-cell notebook in which one 40-character value appears eight times in different containers: the first cell's source literal, its stdout stream text, an execute_result text/plain repr, an execute_result application/json object value, the second cell's source literal, its error evalue, the echoed source line in a traceback frame list, and the final traceback frame.
rationale: Each output kind is a separate field with its own representation (a list of lines, a repr string, a JSON object included as-is, an array of frame strings), and a notebook keeps them all. Failure mode: finding the value in the source and leaving the copies in saved outputs, or counting one covered occurrence as full-input success. Every occurrence gets its own span, labelled by the variable name on the same line. Only the container diversity is this case's own reasoning: the general repeated-occurrence and separate-span rule is the existing multiple-credentials-per-input scenario. The traceback frames are authored plain text; whether a real kernel adds terminal colour codes or a different frame layout is not cited and not claimed.

expectation.rationale: Flag all eight occurrences. The notebook format documents each container: stream text, execute_result and display_data data keyed by MIME type with application/json data included as-is (not double-serialized), and an error output with ename, evalue and a traceback list of frames each a string. The secret status of the value is the IAM user guide statement; the repetition across containers is the authored premise. Synthetic and never issued: each value was built from an authored stem (SYNTHETIC plus a role word plus NEVERISSUED), zero padding and a fixed tail so that it matches the 40-character shape but is not a value any AWS account issued; no notebook was executed, so every output block is authored text, not a recording.

sources.supports: display_data and execute_result carry data keyed by MIME type; application/json data is included as-is; an error output has ename, evalue and a traceback that is a list of frames each represented as a string.
The same output descriptions appear in the 5.2.0 page, including application/json no longer double-serialized since nbformat 4.0.
error requires ename, evalue and traceback (an array of strings); execute_result and display_data hold a mimebundle in which mime-type keys matching application/(.*+)?json may hold any JSON value.
access key = ID + secret used together; secret retrievable only at creation; do not provide access keys to unauthorized parties
